Round 393 is planned and dispatched: **PERF-13c-i**, where previewing a demo MP3 in the library streams it instead of decoding the whole file. Decision is **CONTINUE**; nothing in `store/` was changed by me.

**Round 392 result.** C passed in a real browser at both viewports with 0 bugs, and the gate published it as `c1183a0`. So:
- PERF-13b-ii is done.
- C-R391-01 is closed: a replaced or stopped preview no longer leaves "Loading…" on the status line.
- The round-392 task is preserved as `tasks/round-392.md`, and the backlog is now v360.

**Why PERF-13c next.** I measured HEAD in Chromium first:

| Preview | Decode time | Extra memory | First sound |
|---|---|---|---|
| Middle East | 278 ms | +37.1 MiB | 360 ms |
| Hero | 673 ms | +55.1 MiB | 765 ms |
| Synth sources (already in memory) | none | none | 66 ms |

**What round 393 does.**
- **Stream path:** a source that has finished loading, is no longer held in memory and has a URL plays through a plain `HTMLAudioElement`. It does no decode and adds no memory.
- **Status line:** nothing is written while it buffers.
- **Fallback:** if the stream fails, it falls back to the existing decode path with the round-392 status texts, and remembers that per collection.
- **Unchanged:** synth sources keep today's behaviour.
- **A's tests:** 15 jsdom rows, PS1–PS15, each naming a mutation it must catch.
- **C's checks:** 11 browser rows (S1–S11) at 1440×900 and 1280×720, plus the perf resources run, the auth check, the source-scope check and doc 252.

**My sketch already works in Chromium at both viewports.** Middle East streamed with 0 decodes and memory unchanged. Stop released the element, and blocking the media request fell back to the decode path correctly. Before dispatch I also ran:
- the full suite on the sketch (257 files, 3801 tests). My mutation runs overlapped that run, so it isn't clean evidence on its own;
- the 14 covering test files again on the final sketch (238 tests), clean;
- seven mutations, all caught by the sketch tests;
- a tech-lead review and a re-review of the 4-line change made after it.

**Decisions you may want to look at:**
- **One deferred Medium:** a stalled stream that never recovers. I moved its fix to the next stage, PERF-13c-ii. It stays listed as an open Medium so root can see it and may overrule. Round 393 streams only the demo's own same-origin files, which carry the same hung-fetch risk as today's decode path.
- **Purchased sources** are left to PERF-13c-ii. Their browser check needs the backend, so it will be BLOCKED in the cloud, never PASS.
- **Architecture checkpoint for the decode code:** root still hasn't answered, so I ruled "keep it where it is". The A reviewer, the gate reviewer and tech-lead all said the same, and the new code goes in `preview.client.ts`. The request stays open for root to confirm.
- **A-R392-REVIEW-M1** (a false "is ready" after the collection changes): rated Low. It can't happen today because only `/studio-lab` mounts the workspace, with a fixed collection. It is now a required row in SRW-21-PLAN.
- Five new Lows from round 392 went to the deferred polish list.

**Housekeeping:**
- **Stray folder:** for about 30 seconds my scratch dev server ran without its separate Vite cache. It left a stray folder, `store/node_modules/.vite/deps_temp_d4b0a7e9`. The store server on :5173 still loads the Studio normally (checked with a fresh browser load, no server errors). I didn't delete the folder; root can remove it.
- **Consults:** the advisor was available and used before and after writing. performance-optimizer and tech-lead were both consulted, as the perf rules require.
- **Timing:** the next regression round is due on or after 2026-11-10, and the RETRO is at round 400.
